overview: Italy is a country in southern Europe, made up of a boot-shaped peninsula and the islands of Sicily and Sardinia. Its capital, Rome, was the centre of the Roman Empire and surrounds Vatican City. Italy was unified into one kingdom in 1861. It was a founding member of what is now the European Union, and it is famous around the world for its art, architecture, food and fashion.

geography.text: The Alps form Italy's northern border, and the Apennine Mountains run down the length of the peninsula. Between them lies the Po Valley, the country's largest plain and its main farming region. Italy has active volcanoes, including Mount Etna on Sicily and Vesuvius near Naples. Two tiny independent countries, San Marino and Vatican City, lie entirely inside Italy.

history.text: Rome grew from a small city into an empire that ruled the whole Mediterranean. After it fell, Italy was split into many states, and cities such as Florence and Venice led the Renaissance in art and science. Italy was unified in 1861, became a fascist dictatorship under Benito Mussolini in the 1920s, and voted to become a republic in 1946.

events.title: Founding of Rome
events.text: The traditional date for the founding of Rome.

events.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.text: The last Western Roman emperor is removed from power.

events.title: The Renaissance
events.text: Florence becomes the centre of a rebirth of art and learning.

events.title: Unification
events.text: Most of the Italian peninsula is united as the Kingdom of Italy.

events.title: Mussolini takes power
events.text: The fascist leader becomes prime minister and then dictator.

events.title: Republic
events.text: Italians vote to end the monarchy.

government.text: Italy is a parliamentary republic. Its parliament has two chambers, the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate, and the government is led by the Prime Minister. The President is elected by parliament for seven years. Italy was a founding member of what is now the European Union and of NATO.

economy.text: Italy has one of the largest economies in Europe. The north is highly industrial, making machinery, cars and luxury goods, with brands such as Ferrari, Fiat, Gucci and Prada. Food and wine, from pasta and parmesan to olive oil, are exported worldwide, and Italy is one of the most visited countries on Earth.

culture.text: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country. It was the heart of the Renaissance, home to artists such as Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo and Raphael, and the birthplace of opera. Pizza and pasta, born in Italy, are eaten across the world.

items.title: The Colosseum
items.text: Rome's giant amphitheatre, opened in AD 80.

items.title: Opera
items.text: Born in Italy around 1600; Italian opera singing is listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Venice
items.text: A city built on more than 100 small islands in a lagoon.

sport.text: Football is a passion in Italy. The men's team has won the World Cup four times and the European Championship twice. Italy also has a great cycling tradition with the Giro d'Italia, and Ferrari is the oldest and most successful team in Formula 1.

items.title: Giro d'Italia
items.text: One of cycling's three great races, held since 1909.
Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo hosted the Winter Olympics.
